**Synopsis:**
The Indian rupee posted a strong gain, closing at a 10-week high, driven by larger-than-expected NRI deposit inflows under the RBI's special scheme. The RBI, already holding a ~$137B forward short position, is now seen shifting toward active two-way USD/INR management rather than purely defensive rupee support. Near-term headwinds include importer dollar demand, elevated and rising oil prices linked to U.S.-Iran military tensions, widening India's trade deficit. On the U.S. side, the 10-year Treasury yield is near a 3-year high at ~4.78%, with Fed rate hike odds for September at ~63%, reinforcing a globally hawkish backdrop.
